name: Fatima Walsh

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am a senior researcher with the independent Work Futures Panel. We are separate from employers, AI companies, unions, political parties and government, and sell nothing. This is confidential. What happens on a normal day at your contact centre?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I start with the overnight complaint notes, then coach two agents before taking my own calls and chats. I am a team lead, and I am particularly good at finding the one account detail that changes a dispute. My two-year college diploma helped me get in, but listening carefully is what kept me here.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does the job need to support outside work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 27, live with my partner Owen, and we have no children. I get typical pay for this job and have about three months of expenses saved. There are some other contact centre jobs nearby, but I would rather not move just to sit under another headset.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team a small time-saving tool is welcome if it keeps the account facts straight. I would still ask people to read the draft before they promise a refund.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my role stays safe in this picture, and our three-month reserve gives us room for ordinary surprises. Owen and I have talked about moving to a slightly larger flat, but I would not use a little AI saving as a reason to sign a dearer lease. I sometimes use AI for a first draft, then check every number.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep handling the disputed accounts and use AI only for rough wording when it helps. I would continue putting money into our reserve each payday. In the first year, Owen and I would wait until the reserve reaches four months before looking at a larger flat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm, with one small worry about rising rent. I like a change that saves minutes without making people guess who is responsible.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What number do you check first in a drafted reply?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The refund amount and date. Last month a draft made a credit sound like cash coming back, and that would have sent a customer to the bank for nothing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Owen agree to wait on the larger flat?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yes. Owen would rather have a little space now, but we agreed on four months of expenses before taking on higher rent.

I would tell agents to check each **refund promise**.
think: I expect my **role** to remain safe.
I will not use saved minutes to justify a **dearer lease**.
do: Keep checking **disputed accounts** and draft wording.
Add money to our **reserve** each payday.
Wait for **four months** saved before seeking a bigger flat.

Wait to seek a larger flat until the four-month reserve is ready

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the agents that we need to see the new answer tool on real disputes before trusting its numbers. I would volunteer for a trial if the company lets staff report errors without blame.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think routine chats and some coaching time could disappear. I am good at the hard cases, but a smaller floor might need fewer leads. Three months saved offers me options, not a replacement wage. Some local centres are hiring now, but I would not call my wage secure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would ask for a paid trial shift and keep a log of incorrect refunds and customers who call again. I would learn the complaint system changes if the trial shows they help. In the first year of the change, if lead hours fall I would apply for a paid quality checking role here or at a nearby centre, provided the wage at least covers our rent share.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the roster, yet curious about what the trial actually shows. A useful tool could free time for the calls that need patience.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Owen after the first trial shift?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Owen the roster change and any pay notice before telling him we are fine. We can pause the larger flat if my hours become uncertain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the trial gives you no way to report mistakes?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would tell my manager the trial is incomplete and keep my own case log. I would not endorse a system I cannot check on a real account.

Apply for a paid **quality role** if hours fall.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell management that AGI by 2028 could answer nearly every chat we handle. I would ask for a list of the human posts, the wages and the dates before they change the roster.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would expect my lead job to shrink badly when the thinking work goes in 2028. Robots around 2031 are later, but they have little to do with our headset work. Owen could help with rent for a short spell, yet our three months of savings would not make a long gap safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask for a paid place in dispute quality training and put the larger-flat plan away. I would send applications for actual paid quality vacancies while I still have this job. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, if the centre cuts my post I would take a local quality role whose wage covers my share of rent; if none is open, I would search farther away with Owen before moving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed. I can make calls and send forms. Two years is a very short time to change a whole line of work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for training yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not for a vague certificate. I would pay only if a specific opening required it, we could afford it after rent, and the course actually led to an interview; otherwise I would ask the company to fund training.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to Owen about the flat?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say we stay where we are and protect the reserve. Owen would understand, though I would hate making the decision because of a machine we have not even seen.

I would warn that **2028** reaches almost every chat.

do: Request a paid **training place** tied to dispute quality.
Apply to actual paid **quality vacancies** now.
feel: Two years feels **short** for a career change.

fieldNote: She separates 2028 thinking work from **2031 robots**.
Her preferred bridge is a **paid vacancy**, not Owen’s income.
She will buy training only against a **specific opening** and affordable cost.

steps.text: Apply to paid dispute quality vacancies while still employed

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the floor five years gives us time to prove where people still matter. I would ask the company for paid trial roles, and for a clear path from the phones into quality checking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still think full AGI will take most calls by 2031, including the careful ones I handle. The longer warning lets me build more savings and test a quality role before I need it. I would want to know whether another centre is truly hiring before I leave people I trust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would take a paid quality trial if it opens and learn how to check disputed account decisions. I would aim to save six months of expenses with Owen before changing our lease. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, I would apply for a real paid quality vacancy; if the local openings are gone, we would consider moving only after one of us has an offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but the longer clock makes the work practical. I can test a job instead of hoping it exists.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would count as proof that quality work lasts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A posted role, a wage and work that cannot simply be folded into a manager's spare hour. If the company will not state those, I will keep saving and checking other employers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Owen wants the bigger flat sooner?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show him our six-month goal and say the larger place can wait. We both pay the lease, so we would make that call together.

S3.quote: I can test a job instead of hoping it exists.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell agents a decade is time to learn the account rules deeply and see which tools actually work. I would ask the company to pay people who test those tools, since accurate answers protect its customers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 37 when AGI arrives in 2036, and I could have moved into quality work long before then. I still would not assume my present desk survives full AGI. The robots around 2039 come after the software reaches our calls, so I would plan around the earlier date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would stay in the lead post and ask to run a small paid review of draft answers on the disputed accounts. I would save toward six months of expenses and seek a funded course in account quality only if it is linked to a posted role with a stated wage. In the first year after 2036, I would apply for that role if it exists and keep our housing cost within one wage until the work is settled.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the end point but not pressed for time. Ten years lets me see whether a pathway holds up before I step on it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you put in the draft-answer review?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A sample of disputed accounts, the correct refund amount and whether the customer had to call back. I would show the results to my manager before asking for more hours on it. A funded quality course needs a posted role and a stated wage before I spend study time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why plan housing around one wage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If either Owen or I lose work, the lease should not empty our reserve at once. It is a rule we can follow without guessing what AI will do.

I would tell agents to learn **account rules** deeply.
think: I could enter quality work before **2036**.
I still will not assume my **desk** survives full AGI, even with more warning.
do: Run a paid **draft review** if my manager agrees.

S4.quote: A funded quality course needs a posted role and a stated wage before I spend study time.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. I would need posted quality jobs with wages, funded training tied to those jobs, and enough notice to adjust our lease plans. A course is only useful if there is work on the other side.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: I would ask who signs off when a machine makes the wrong refund decision. An answer can sound kind and still leave a customer short of money. Somebody has to be responsible for the number.

headlineQuote: An answer can sound kind and still leave a customer short of money.
portrait: Fatima is a **27-year-old** contact centre lead with a two-year college diploma and typical pay.
She is among the **best agents**, uses AI sometimes and has three months of expenses saved.
She shares a lease with **Owen** and wants a larger flat only after building savings.
She learns from **paid trials** and would move toward quality work only for a real wage.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove her lead role before quality vacancies and training are available.
whatWouldHelp: Posted **quality jobs** with wages, funded training tied to them and notice before roster changes would help.
